title: Proposal title.

sub_topic: Specific sub-areas this proposal belongs to.

one_sentence_thesis: The contribution in one sentence: under 30 words, no jargon, no metric numbers.

core_problem.problem_statement: 1-2 sentences, specific about what fails and why.
why_it_matters: Motivation only: real-world impact and the gap prior work leaves. Do not describe the solution here.
core_problem.concrete_example: A specific input/output scenario showing what goes wrong with current approaches.

explanation: 2-3 bullets, at most ~35 words each, intuition/analogy level, no formal notation. Name where the borrowed mechanism comes from.
key_novelty.lever: The lever carrying the core bet (objective, representation, architecture, data, inference, interface, formulation or systems; see references/thinking_traps.md), then why it beats the strongest alternative lever.

problem_definition.formal_setting: Mathematical or formal description of the problem.

related_work.sub_area: Name of a line of prior work.
related_work.what_it_does: Mechanism-level summary of that prior work, with inline [id] citations.
related_work.open_gap: The gap this line of work leaves that the proposal addresses.

high_level_flow: Stage name: module A -> module B -> module C
novel_architectural_elements: Structural design choices only: how modules are arranged or connected in a way prior work does not.
method.pseudocode: The core algorithm as a code-block string.
design_choices: A key design choice and why it is made.
method.theoretical_grounding: Why the mechanism should work here: the transferred principle, the shared structure with the source setting, and any formal argument.

model_details.base_model: Be specific (e.g. 'Llama-3.1-8B'), or 'none — <why the method needs no model>'.

training.method: e.g. supervised fine-tuning, RL, contrastive learning, or 'training-free'.

proposed_evaluation.evaluation_setting: How the method would be evaluated.

falsifiable_predictions.kind: upside | mechanism | safety | cost. At least one upside prediction on the problem's standard metric; safety and cost together at most half.
falsifiable_predictions.prediction: One empirical claim the method implies (a prediction, not a result).
falsifiable_predictions.kill_condition: The observation that would falsify it.

limitations: 3-5 concise limitations, acknowledged or apparent from the method.
